canva.role: Online design platform with templates, a graphic editor and AI tools for creating and editing.
canva.audience: Students, creators, small businesses and marketing teams making posts, presentations, landing pages and branding material without professional design skills.
pros: Hebrew interface: Hebrew (he-IL) is in the list of languages Canva is available in, per developer docs. The help center says picking a local language unlocks local fonts and templates.

Canva AI 2.0, design by conversation: per the press release it supports creating and editing in chat, with memory, external-service connections, scheduling and web research. Launched as a preview from 16 April.
Among the most widely used tools: Canva is #3 on a list of AI websites and #4 on a16z's app list (January 2026 data).
cons: Canva AI 2.0 launched as a limited preview: for the first million users, expanding gradually. The announcement doesn't say which plans include it.
Prices and quotas not verified: Canva's pricing and education pages didn't load, so there are no prices, AI quotas or commercial-use terms here.
canva.privacy: Not verified. The Canva AI 2.0 press release describes training Canva's models but doesn't address use of user content.
canva.api: Yes. Official developer docs (canva.dev) for building Canva apps and extensions. Access prices and terms not checked.
canva.hebrew: Hebrew (he-IL) is in Canva's supported-language list in the developer docs. The help center explains how to pick a language and says a local language unlocks local fonts and templates, but lists no languages.
canva.students: Not verified: the Canva for Education page didn't load, so eligibility and what's included were not checked.

looka.role: AI logo and brand-identity generator, with a brand kit, branded templates and a website builder.
looka.audience: Small-business owners, entrepreneurs and students who need a logo and basic brand identity fast without a designer.
pros: Full ownership of a purchased logo: per the help center, the purchased logo belongs to the user for any commercial or non-commercial use. Ownership stays after a Brand Kit subscription ends.
Brand kit with 300+ templates: Brand Kit at 96 USD/year gives 300+ branded templates generated from your logo, colors and fonts. Brand Kit Web at 129 USD/year adds a website builder with hosting.
Vector files in the Premium package: Premium Logo includes high-resolution PNG, PDF, EPS and SVG for print, transparent versions and black-and-white versions.
cons: No copyright on logo components: copyright covers the logo as a whole, not the icons and fonts, which come from a library and aren't removed from it after purchase. Looka gives no official document; trademark registration needs a lawyer.
Basic package is limited to one file: one 1000x1000 px PNG with a colored background, low resolution.
Business name can't be changed after purchase: on Premium you can edit and re-download, but not edit the name field after purchase.
looka.price: Brand Kit is 96 USD/year. One-time logo package prices not verified.
plans: High-resolution PNG, PDF, EPS and SVG, transparent, black and white versions, lifetime tech support.
300+ branded templates from your logo, colors, fonts and stock photos.
Everything in Brand Kit plus a website builder with hosting and design.
looka.rights: Per the help center, a purchased logo has full ownership and commercial and non-commercial use is allowed. Copyright covers the logo as a whole, not the library icons and fonts.
looka.students: No official student discount found on the pages checked.

adobe-express.role: Adobe's design app for graphics, short video, presentations and web pages, with templates and Firefly tools.
adobe-express.audience: Students, creators and small businesses who need fast graphics, short videos and presentations, plus teachers and pupils in education.
pros: AI tools announced at MAX 2026: per the 11 Oct 2026 blog, a chat AI assistant (beta), web page generation (beta), Extract Brand building a brand kit from PDFs or images (beta) and Brand Check.
Free plan with daily creations: Adobe Express Free costs nothing, no credit card, with free daily creations in some features, 5GB storage and 345,000+ templates.
Export to PSD and IDML files (beta), and Express runs inside Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot and Gemini through an Adobe connector.
cons: 250 credits a month on Premium: Adobe Express Premium includes 250 generation credits a month. The 4,000-credit quota needs Adobe Firefly Pro.
Most new tools are beta: the assistant, web page generation, Extract Brand and Brand Check are marked beta, and the blog doesn't say which plans include them.
adobe-express.price: From S$13.39/month (Premium, Singapore dollars incl. VAT) with a 30-day trial. Free plan with daily creations.
adobe-express.free: Adobe Express Free: no cost, no credit card, free daily creations in some features (amount not stated), 5GB storage and 345,000+ templates.
adobe-express.trial: Premium: 30-day free trial. Firefly Pro: 7-day trial. Billing starts at the end of the trial.
plans: Free daily creations in some features, 5GB storage, 345,000+ templates.
Adobe Express Premium and 250 generation credits/month. Free for eligible K-12 schools.
adobe-express.privacy: Per the Firefly FAQ, for Express's AI engine: 'we don't train on any Creative Cloud subscribers' personal content'. Adobe Stock contributor content is used for training under the contributor agreement. The source refers to Creative Cloud subscribers and doesn't explicitly mention free Express users.
adobe-express.rights: Per the Firefly FAQ, output from non-beta features may be used in commercial projects, and beta output too unless the product says otherwise.
adobe-express.api: Not verified. The blog mentions an Adobe creativity connector that lets you use Express from Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot and Gemini. No Express API docs were checked.
adobe-express.hebrew: Not mentioned in source: no interface-language list or right-to-left note on the Adobe Express pages checked.
adobe-express.students: Per the pricing page, Adobe Express Premium is free for eligible K-12 teachers, and students are told 'You might already have free access to Adobe Express Premium through your school'. For higher education, contact the institution.

recraft.role: Image and vector generator for design, with a vector editor, custom styles and an API.
recraft.audience: Designers and students who need illustrations, icons and logos in vector format, plus developers integrating image generation via API.
pros: Vector output on all plans: per the docs, vector generation and the vector editor are on every plan including free, and the V4 model is available to all. A vector in Recraft V4.1 costs 4 credits.
Relatively cheap Basic plan: 12 USD/month, or 10 USD/month billed annually, with 1,000 credits a month. An image in V4.1 costs 2 credits.
Separate API for programmatic use, with unit pricing separate from Studio credits; API input and output are never used for training.
cons: On the free plan images belong to Recraft: free-plan images are public in the community gallery, owned by Recraft and not licensed for commercial use.
Content is used for training by default: on Free and Pro, images, uploads and prompts are used for training. Free has no opt-out; Pro can opt out in profile settings.
Commercial rights depend on the subscription: on paid plans commercial rights apply to images created during the subscription.
recraft.price: From 12 USD/month billed monthly, or 10 USD/month billed annually. Free plan with daily credits, no commercial use.
recraft.free: Free plan with credits that reset daily (amount not stated in the source). Includes vector generation and the vector editor. Images are public, owned by Recraft and not for commercial use.
plans: Credits reset daily (amount not stated), includes vector generation and vector editor.
1,000 credits/month, private generation, commercial rights during the subscription.
recraft.privacy: Per the docs, Recraft uses user content for training, including generated or uploaded images and prompt text. On Free there is no opt-out. On Pro training is on by default and can be turned off in profile settings ('Help improve Recraft'). On Team opt-out is on by default. API input and output are never used for training.
recraft.rights: On paid plans the user gets full ownership and commercial rights to images created during the subscription, and they stay private after cancelling. On the free plan images belong to Recraft and are not for commercial use.
recraft.api: Yes. API for programmatic access with unit pricing separate from Studio credits. API price list not read.
recraft.watch: Users report refusal of refunds after using more than 30 credits, and credits spent on failed generations.

kittl.role: Online graphic editor with templates, typography and AI image and vector generation, mainly for t-shirts, products and marketing.
kittl.audience: Independent designers, print-on-demand creators and small businesses who need graphics, typography and marketing material.
pros: Broad commercial license on paid plans: Pro and Expert include a commercial license up to 500,000 copies. Per the help center, you can sell designs on physical and digital products without a quantity limit, but not as stock material.

Brand management and one-click variations: the June 2026 update added Brand for managing logo, colors and fonts, Remix Styles for generating variations as an image or editable vector, and Ideogram 4 support.
Daily credits on higher plans: Expert gets 200 credits a day and Max 600, reset every 24 hours and used before the monthly quota.
cons: Free plan limited for commercial use: per the pricing page, Free is for personal use only. The help center allows selling by Free users if they add 'provided by Kittl', and their AI images go into a public library.
Monthly credits don't carry over: unused monthly credits don't roll to the next month. Quota size isn't stated on the pricing page.
kittl.price: Pro from 15 USD per editor per month billed monthly, or 12 USD/month (144 USD/year) billed annually. Free plan for personal use.
kittl.free: Permanent free plan with selected templates and tools and a preview of Pro features with usage limits. The source doesn't say whether it has renewing AI credits.
plans: Selected templates and tools, a taste of most Pro features with limits.
Monthly credits (amount not stated), commercial license up to 500,000 copies, vector and high-quality export.
Monthly credits plus 200 credits a day, commercial license up to 500,000 copies, option to buy extra credits.
Monthly credits plus 600 credits a day, commercial license, option to buy extra credits.
kittl.privacy: Not verified. The help-center rights page doesn't address training on user content.
kittl.rights: Pro and Expert users own the images they create in Kittl AI and can sell designs on physical and digital products without a quantity limit and use them for client work, but not as stock.
kittl.api: Not verified. The blog mentions Kittl MCP, but the page wasn't read and no API docs were found.
kittl.hebrew: Not mentioned in source (the blog says the Ideogram 4 model added to Kittl is strong at multilingual text, languages not listed).
kittl.students: The pricing page mentions no student or education discount.

microsoft-designer.role: Microsoft's free design app for creating posts, invitations, cards and AI images.
microsoft-designer.audience: Private users and students who want quick personal graphics for free, especially those already using Microsoft 365.
microsoft-designer.status: Active. Designer features are also built into Microsoft apps such as Photos, Word and PowerPoint, and credits are shared across Microsoft's AI features.
pros: Free with monthly credits: a free tier with monthly credits for creating and editing, renewed at the start of each month. Each Copilot action costs one credit.
On web and mobile: designer.microsoft.com and iOS and Android apps.
Microsoft 365 raises the quota: Personal, Family and Premium give the account owner up to 4x credits in Designer, alongside Office apps.
cons: Personal-use license only: per the FAQ, Designer is licensed 'for personal, non-commercial use' with a Microsoft account.
Free credit amount not published: the page mentions monthly credits without a number, and on a family account the boost applies to the subscription owner only.
Text in images may come out in another language: the FAQ warns that text in generated images may not appear in the language you asked for.
microsoft-designer.price: Free with monthly credits. More credits via Microsoft 365 Personal from 9.99 USD/month or 99.99 USD/year.
microsoft-designer.model: Free, expandable via a Microsoft 365 subscription
microsoft-designer.free: Designer is free to use, with monthly credits renewed at the start of each month. Each Copilot action costs one credit. Credit amount not stated.
plans: Monthly credits for creating and editing (amount not stated).
Up to 4x Designer credits for the account owner, Microsoft 365 apps.
Up to 4x Designer credits for the account owner, Microsoft 365 apps.
Up to 4x Designer credits for the account owner, extensive image generation in Copilot.
microsoft-designer.privacy: Per the FAQ, prompts and answers are collected to investigate abuse, and Microsoft uses data 'to provide, support and improve' the service. The source doesn't say explicitly whether content is used to train models.
microsoft-designer.rights: Per the FAQ, Designer is licensed for personal, non-commercial use with a Microsoft account. The source doesn't distinguish free accounts from subscribers.
microsoft-designer.hebrew: Not mentioned in source (the product page says availability varies by device and language, without listing languages).
microsoft-designer.students: No dedicated student benefit found on the pages checked.

adobe-illustrator.role: Adobe's vector graphics software for logos, illustrations and visual identity, with Firefly tools and an AI agent in beta.
adobe-illustrator.audience: Visual-communication students and professional designers building logos, illustrations and visual identities in vector files.
pros: Discounted price for students: Creative Cloud Pro, which includes Illustrator and 4,000 generation credits a month, is offered to students and teachers at a discount. A Black Friday sale of 76% off the first year was running.
AI agent inside the app: per the 10 Nov 2026 announcement, Adobe Creative Agent is in beta in Illustrator, alongside new on-canvas Blend controls and refreshed content libraries.

Firefly output allowed for commercial use: per the Firefly FAQ, output from non-beta features may be used in commercial projects, and Adobe says it doesn't train on Creative Cloud subscribers' personal content.
cons: Few generation credits on the single-app plan: the Illustrator-only plan includes 25 generation credits a month. 4,000 credits need Creative Cloud Pro.
Annual subscription: all plans shown are annual, billed monthly; no monthly option without commitment was shown.
adobe-illustrator.price: Illustrator from Ch$ 15,640/month (Chilean pesos, before VAT) on an annual plan billed monthly. No free plan; 7-day trial.
adobe-illustrator.trial: 7-day free trial for personal plans and 14 days for team plans.
plans: Illustrator and Creative Cloud apps, 4,000 generation credits/month, 100GB storage.
Same as Creative Cloud Pro: 4,000 credits/month, 100GB storage.
adobe-illustrator.privacy: Per the Firefly FAQ: 'we don't train on any Creative Cloud subscribers' personal content'. Adobe Stock contributor content is used for training under the contributor agreement.
adobe-illustrator.rights: Per the Firefly FAQ, output from non-beta features may be used commercially, and beta output too unless stated otherwise. A commercial license doesn't guarantee protection against copyright claims.
adobe-illustrator.api: Not verified. Adobe announced a local MCP connection letting external agents work in Illustrator, in a private beta planned for early 2027; not yet available at check time.
adobe-illustrator.students: The plans page offers Creative Cloud Pro (incl. Illustrator) to students and teachers at a discount; a Black Friday sale of 76% off the first year, Ch$ 10,875/month, ran until Nov 27. Eligibility is checked separately.

lovart.role: AI design agent that creates designs on a canvas from a free-language request.
lovart.audience: Designers and creators who want to try a design agent that produces graphics from a description, alongside their usual tools.
pros: You can start free: the pricing page offers a free plan ('Get started for free'). Its details aren't in the page text.
Purchased credits are valid for a year: add-on credits are valid for 366 days from purchase.
Unlimited slow generation on some plans: some plans have Unlimited Relax Generation, a slow queue that uses no credits, for a fixed period such as 31 or 180 days.
cons: Monthly credits don't roll over: on monthly and annual plans alike, credits reset each month and unused ones are lost.
Free generation is a one-time perk: Unlimited Relax Generation is given once per account, for a fixed period, and only on certain plans.
Connection limit per account: up to 2 desktop browser connections and 1 mobile browser connection per account. Multiple users need the Team plan.
lovart.price: Not stated on the pricing page text.
lovart.free: A free plan exists, but its quotas don't appear in the pricing page text.
plans: Per the page description: advanced capabilities, larger volume and commercial projects.
lovart.privacy: The privacy policy (23 July 2025) doesn't address training models on user content.
lovart.rights: Per the pricing page description, Pro is meant for 'commercial projects' among other uses. Usage rights per plan weren't verified from the terms. This is no guarantee against copyright claims.
lovart.students: No student benefit found on the official pages checked.
